title: AWR/2 WorkReceipt
description: NON-NORMATIVE. JSON Schema is a convenience for tooling and is not the normative definition of AWR/2; awr/SPEC.md is (Appendix B). Where this schema and the specification disagree, the schema is the bug. A WorkReceipt answers what happened: which model, over which input, producing which output, at what cost (SPEC.md §3.3). Passing this schema is necessary but far from sufficient for validity — see the $comment below.
$comment: This schema checks structure only. It cannot check the Ed25519 proof (AWR-PROOF-006), the did:key/verificationMethod agreement (AWR-PROOF-007), parent digests (AWR-CHAIN-003), timestamp ordering (AWR-RCPT-003), duplicate property names (AWR-CANON-004), or SPEC.md §4.3's global prohibition on non-integer JSON numbers — the last is unenforceable in JSON Schema both because §3.1 allows unknown properties at any level (a float under an unknown property is unreachable from any subschema) and because "type": "integer" tests the mathematical value, so `"latencyMs": 2340.0` passes it. Where a number-valued member IS named, this schema pins "type": "integer" with the §4.3 bounds of [-(2^53-1), 2^53-1], and the validator must still do the rest. The full list of non-expressible requirements is in common-v2.json's file-level $comment. Never set additionalProperties:false on any object here: §3.1 requires unknown properties to be preserved, and stripping them invalidates the signature.

type.$comment: SPEC.md §3.1: `type` MUST be an array containing `VerifiableCredential` (AWR-DOC-004) and exactly one AWR type from {WorkReceipt, VerificationVerdict, BlameAttestation} (AWR-DOC-005). Further types MAY be present, so the array is not closed and no positional constraint is imposed. "Exactly one" is expressed as: contains WorkReceipt, and contains neither of the other two.

modelId.$comment: SPEC.md §3.3: MUST be present and non-empty (AWR-RCPT-005). The form <model>@<vendor> is RECOMMENDED but explicitly not constrained — it is an opaque label chosen by the issuer — so no pattern is imposed. §14: a voluntary disclosure that SHOULD be omitted where it leaks vendor relationships.

capability.$comment: Appears in the SPEC.md §3.3 example but is described nowhere in the prose, has no reason code, and is in no required list. Typed as a string here and left OPTIONAL and unconstrained — see the report finding: §3.3 does not define this member.

startedAt.$comment: SPEC.md §3.3: OPTIONAL — the ordering rule is written for "when both are present". MUST NOT be later than `work.completedAt` (AWR-RCPT-003), which is a cross-field comparison and not expressible here.

completedAt.$comment: SPEC.md §3.3: MUST be present and MUST be an RFC 3339 UTC date-time (AWR-RCPT-003).

latencyMs.$comment: SPEC.md §3.3: MUST, if present, be a non-negative integer (§4.3, AWR-RCPT-004). Upper bound is §4.3's 2^53-1.

status.$comment: SPEC.md §3.3: MUST be one of these five values (AWR-RCPT-006). A receipt for work that did not succeed is a first-class document — an unverifiable failure is the case a dispute most often turns on — so nothing here privileges `succeeded`.

inputDigest.$comment: SPEC.md §3.3: MUST be present and MUST be an SRI string as in §3.2 (AWR-RCPT-001). This digests APPLICATION PAYLOAD bytes, not an AWR document: the issuer chooses the payload serialization and SHOULD document it. §14: for a low-entropy payload the digest is a confirmation oracle, and the issuer SHOULD salt the hashed bytes.

outputDigest.$comment: SPEC.md §3.3: MUST be present, same rules as inputDigest. A receipt for status "failed" MUST still carry an outputDigest; the digest of the empty byte string is permitted.

parents.$comment: SPEC.md §3.3 and §8: OPTIONAL; when present MUST be an array of digest references, each of which MAY carry a `role`. No minItems: §3.3 does not forbid an empty array. Chain rules — DAG, cycle detection (AWR-CHAIN-004), depth/node limits defaulting to 64 and 1024 (AWR-CHAIN-005), conflicting digests for the same id (AWR-CHAIN-006), parent outputDigest vs child inputDigest (AWR-CHAIN-007, warning) — are graph properties over other documents and none of them is expressible in JSON Schema. §8.2: a verifier MUST NOT fetch a parent from the network.

price.$comment: SPEC.md §3.3: OPTIONAL (AWR-RCPT-002). `amount` MUST NOT be a JSON number (§4.3).

nonce.$comment: SPEC.md §3.3: OPTIONAL but RECOMMENDED — it is what makes two receipts over identical input and output distinguishable, and what a replay check keys on. The §3.3 example is a ULID, but no syntax is specified, so only "type": "string" is asserted.

environment.$comment: SPEC.md §3.3 and §7: OPTIONAL, members opaque. Presence of an unverified attestation is AWR-ENV-001 (warning) and MUST NOT make the document count as more trustworthy (§7.3).

settlement.$comment: SPEC.md §3.3 and §10.3: OPTIONAL; one of the two accountability bindings profile L2 accepts (AWR-PROFILE-004). Presence is never on-chain-checked during verification (AWR-L2-001, warning).

awrProfile.$comment: SPEC.md §3.3: OPTIONAL, a non-binding hint. A verifier MUST NOT grant a level because a document claims it.
